subject: MAP: POC environment checklist & dependencies (VPC, SSO, KMS)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: POC environment checklist & dependencies (VPC, SSO, KMS)

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed MAP milestones for the POC environment so we can get aligned on owners and target dates. I attached a draft MAP (redwood_map_draft_v1.pdf) and a working Drive link here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=MAP-ACME-POC-2026

Proposed MAP milestone: POC environment setup (owner / dependencies / target):
- VPC peering / network connectivity — Owner: Acme infra (action: create peering request, provide VPC CIDR(s) and peering contact). Redwood will provide peer VPC ID and routing guidance. Target: 2026-03-02
- IP allowlist and NAT egress IPs — Owner: Acme security (action: provide egress IPs to allow). Redwood will share service IPs and ports. Target: 2026-03-02
- SSO / SAML integration — Owner: Acme identity + Redwood SSO eng (action: exchange metadata, configure IdP). Need Okta metadata file or SAML entityID/ACS URLs. Target: 2026-03-04
- Secrets / KMS access for POC — Owner: Acme security + Redwood ops (action: decide whether to use Acme KMS or Redwood-managed secrets; provide KMS key policy if Acme-managed). Target: 2026-03-04
- Test accounts & sample data scope — Owner: Acme product + Redwood CSM. Target: 2026-03-05

Open asks for your team: please share
1) Primary network contact for the peering work (name/email)
2) VPC CIDR(s) you plan to peer and any peering restrictions (route tables, restricted subnets)
3) Okta metadata or the SAML metadata URL
4) Any procurement/whitelisting steps we should include in the MAP (security questionnaires, egress IP approvals)

I'll coordinate internal engineering (Nikhil) to follow up on the technical details once we have the contact + CIDR. If these dates look tight on your side we can stretch, but we'd like to start the POC week of Mar 2 to hit a mid-March POC close.

Thanks — attaching MAP draft and a short one-page VPC requirements doc.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: MAP: POC environment checklist & dependencies (VPC, SSO, KMS)

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming next steps from Acme side and answers to your asks:

1) Network contact: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com> (CC'd on this thread). Priya will own the peering and routing tasks.
2) VPC CIDR slated for peering: 10.52.0.0/16 (dev-poc) and 10.53.0.0/16 (shared-services). We can open the peering request once Redwood provides the peer VPC ID and a short requirements doc. I'm also attaching a network diagram (acme_network_requirements_v1.png).
3) SSO: we use Okta. I'll ask our IdP team to share Okta metadata — expect to provide entityID, ACS URLs and cert in the next 48 hours.
4) Procurement/whitelisting: security will need the egress IPs and an internal security questionnaire filled out (we use a short vendor checklist). We can share that once our security ops person reviews the MAP.

On KMS: we prefer to use Acme-managed KMS for secrets in the POC. We'll need Redwood to provide a recommended IAM policy for the KMS key so our security team can review.

Proposed dates look reasonable. We can target a POC start the week of Mar 2 and aim to complete the POC by Mar 18. I've looped Priya — Priya, will you confirm the timeline and whether the network team needs a call to walk through routing?

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Director, Platform Engineering — Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 08:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: POC environment checklist & dependencies (VPC, SSO, KMS)

Hi Priya / Alex — copy of a few technical requirements from Redwood side to make the peering and allowlist straightforward:

- Peering model: AWS VPC Peering preferred (no transit gateway) for the POC. We'll provide our peer VPC ID and a list of subnets that will host the inference nodes.
- Routing: Please add routes for the Redwood subnets to the dev-poc route table (10.52.0.0/16) once peering is accepted. We will not require overlapping CIDRs.
- Ports: Required outbound: 443 (API/agent), 5228 (health/tracing)/HTTPS fallback — recommend allowing outbound TCP 443 and 5228. Inbound rules are not required from Acme to Redwood for the standard flow; if you plan to use inbound callbacks we can document the minimal ports.
- NAT/Egress IPs: If your VPC uses NAT, please provide the set of egress IPs that will be seen by external services so we can whitelist them on our side. Alternatively we can provide a set of static Redwood IPs to add to your allowlist.
- SAML: we'll need the IdP metadata XML or entityID + ACS URL. Required attributes: email, name, groups (optional). We support Okta out-of-the-box.
- KMS/Secrets: For Acme-managed KMS, please provide the KMS key ARN and the IAM principal you'd like Redwood to use (we can use a short-lived service account flow). If you prefer Redwood-managed secrets, we'll provide the integration details and a service principal for limited access.

I've attached a short VPC requirements markdown that covers the above and includes sample IAM policy snippets for KMS. Happy to jump on a 30-min sync with Priya and our infra engineer to unblock the peering.

Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_vpc_requirements.md (text/markdown, 8 KB)
